stem:
The diagram shows Krish's clay brick resting on the floor. The brick does not slide or tip. Two forces on the brick are labelled: the downward pull of Earth and the upward push of the floor.

Krish asks what this shows about forces on an object at rest.

parts.text: Which claim about the forces on the brick is correct?

options.text: Balanced forces act on the brick, including the push between the floor and the brick, so it stays at rest.
No force acts on the brick because it is not moving.
An object at rest always has an unbalanced force acting on it.
Stopping the brick automatically makes every force on it vanish.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Rest does not mean zero force; balanced forces can keep the brick still.

teacher.key_rationale: An object at rest can have forces that cancel. The floor pushes up on the brick; that balanced set keeps it still. Not moving does not mean no force, and rest does not require an unbalanced force or vanishing forces.
teacher.figure_note: Brick on floor with upward floor push and downward Earth pull.
